        """The readings: the primary one (Nemotron, a few seconds) and an optional slower second
        one (Gemini) start together on the same receipts. Each is shown as that model's reading;
        neither sets the status. When their calls differ, both are shown and the difference is
        counted (`readings_disagree`), never resolved by picking one."""
        primary, second = self.deps.assessor, self.deps.second_assessor
        with self.lock:
            empty = not self.result.posts and not self.result.pages
        if empty:

            self.skip("second_reading", "nothing was found to read")

        if not primary:
            self.skip("assess", "Nemotron is not configured on this server")
        if not second:
            self.skip("second_reading", "no second reading model on this server")
        if not (primary or second):
            return
        with self.lock:
            snap = self.result.model_copy(deep=True)
        jobs = []
        if primary:
            jobs.append(("assess", primary, self.deadline))
        if second:
            jobs.append(("second_reading", second, time.monotonic() + self.deps.second_reading_s))
        pool = ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=len(jobs), thread_name_prefix="lookup-read")

            futures = [pool.submit(self._reading, sid, m, snap, dl) for sid, m, dl in jobs]
            wait(futures, timeout=max(dl for _, _, dl in jobs) - time.monotonic() + 1.0)
        finally:

SSE_PING_S = 10.0

@router.get("/{job_id}/events")
async def lookup_events(
    job_id: str, request: Request, jobs: Annotated[JobStore, Depends(get_jobs)]
) -> StreamingResponse:
    """The same LookupResult as GET /api/lookup/{id}, pushed as server-sent events: one
    `snapshot` event at once and one whenever the job changes, ending after the snapshot whose
    state is no longer "running". Clients that can't stream fall back to polling."""
    job = jobs.get(job_id)
    if job is None:
        raise HTTPException(404, "unknown or expired lookup id")

    async def stream():

        while True:
            snap = job.snapshot()
            body = json.dumps(snap, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))
            now = time.monotonic()
            if body != last:
                yield f"event: snapshot\\ndata: {body}\\n\\n"
                last, sent_at = body, now
            elif now - sent_at >= SSE_PING_S:
                yield ": ping\\n\\n"

            if snap["state"] != "running" or now - opened > SSE_MAX_S:
                return
            if await request.is_disconnected():

            await asyncio.sleep(SSE_TICK_S)

    return StreamingResponse(

5. Concurrency: a fake Oxylabs whose post-page scrape returns fast but whose author-profile scrape blocks on a threading.Event: copies_x / copies_web start (started_at) before the author step ends. And: verify starts before a slow linked page (card URL) finishes. Use events/barriers, not timing guesses, where possible.
6. Web input: `_page_text` heading starts the searches before `_linked` finishes (the linked fake blocks on an Event until a search has been called); the final page keeps the facts receipt (not the markdown one) and role "linked".
7. verify_max and profiles_max caps hold across the two queue calls; a copier whose account is already read is not read again; only verified posts are copies (existing honesty rule).
8. Cache: CachedOxylabs second identical call doesn't hit the inner client, its receipt has cached=True and the "(cached read" suffix, X metrics_as_of equals the first fetch time; failures are not cached; TTL expiry with an injected clock.
9. SSE endpoint via FastAPI TestClient (see tests/test_api_routes.py / test_lookup.py test_api_validation_and_polling for how the router is mounted and get_jobs overridden): stream of a finished job yields one `event: snapshot` whose data parses to the snapshot and then ends; unknown id -> 404.
10. bsky last_call is per thread.
Run the whole suite at the end (`.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q`), make ruff check/format clean for your files, and report: files created, pass/xfail counts, and any bugs found (with failure scenarios).

Outside lookup/assess.py, no user waits on a Gemini call: `POST /api/analyze` makes none, and the other five call sites run in background workers or offline scripts. So switching to Nemotron would bring no latency gain for users. The only site worth considering is the batch single-shot verdict (#2), and only to free up the hourly Gemini quota. The report is saved at /tmp/claude-1001/-home-dev--t3-worktrees-gemini-4-braincells-feat-nemotron-fast-look-b6fdf3ecdc47167e/bfa758a0-97a2-4ab6-a367-9c178e2053b8/scratchpad/gemini-audit.md. This audit was read-only: I edited no repo files and made no commits.

I ran the brain brief, graph query and graph neighbors as the agent guide asks. The brief's code-context index wasn't built for this commit ("search store not built"), so its source locations came back empty; the graph calls worked. Graph finds only three callers outside lookup: `GeminiAgent` is called from `analyst/runner.py:69` and `analyst/compare.py:97`, `GeminiVerdictModel` from `runner.py:64` and `compare.py:129`, and `GeminiEmbedder` from `signals/__main__.py:112` and `signals/attack_eval.py:175`. Nothing in `api/`, `lookup/`, `sources/` or `media/` imports `analyst/`, except that `lookup/assess.py:125` imports its price table.

## Call sites

| # | Site | What it does / config | Who waits | Latency (documented) | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `analyst/agent.py:146` `GeminiAgent.run` | Per-cluster verdict that can investigate first. Up to 8 tool turns plus 1 forced final turn (`:142-168`). Tools: `search_web` and `scrape_url` (live Oxylabs), `get_cluster_posts` and `get_account` (database). Native function calling, set to AUTO and then NONE on the last turn (`:124`). JSON output against the `VerdictDraft` schema, temperature 0.2, `gemini-4-hydrogen` (`common/config.py:14`). No thinking config is set. | The `analyst` background worker, for coordinated and insufficient clusters (`runner.py:24,83`). | p50 18 s on spam clusters, 29.5 s on news clusters, about $0.04–0.07 per cluster (`analyst/README.md:101,118`) | **Keep on Gemini.** It depends on multi-turn function calling over Oxylabs. A documented comparison of 5 models picked hydrogen because it uses the tools (README `:136-142`). The project runs on a hackathon Gemini key (`ratecap.py:3`). Tool calling on the Verda vLLM endpoint is unverified, and porting the loop would be 150+ lines plus a new comparison run. Propose only. |
| 2 | `analyst/gemini.py:43` `GeminiVerdictModel.draft` | Single-shot verdict on evidence gathered beforehand. Structured output, no tools, `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` (`config.py:15`). | The same worker, for `likely_organic` clusters, which are most of them (`runner.py:5,83`). | p50 1.3 s, $0.0012, agrees with the detector on 14 of 15 clusters (README `:110,148`) | **Could switch; small change (about 60–80 lines).** The `VerdictModel` Protocol (`gemini.py:17-20`) is a clean place to plug in Nemotron, and the verdict pipeline and guard stay as they are. It isn't faster (1.3 s now against about 3 s for Nemotron). The gain is moving these calls off the 100 requests/hour Gemini cap (`config.py:23`). Propose only, after a `compare.py` run. |
| 3 | `analyst/compare.py:97,129` | Offline comparison of 5 Gemini models. Writes nothing to the database. | A developer running it by hand (about 25 min, about $3) | – | **Keep.** If #1 or #2 ever moves, add a Nemotron row here first. |
| 4 | `signals/attack.py:82` (red team) | Writes fictional campaign and organic post sets as JSON fixtures. Schema output, temperature 1.0 / 0.7, hydrogen (`:26`). | Offline command only | not documented | **Keep.** The fixtures must be reproducible, and the semantic signal is calibrated on these Gemini-written sets (`semantic.py:3-4`, `score.py:226`). Swapping means regenerating the fixtures and re-calibrating. |
| 5 | `signals/semantic.py:60` `GeminiEmbedder` | `embed_content` with `gemini-embedding-001`, 768 dimensions, batches of 100. Fails quietly if the call errors. | The `signals` background worker, plus offline `attack_eval.py` | not documented | **Keep.** These are embeddings, not chat: NemotronClient has no embeddings endpoint, and the 0.85 similarity threshold is calibrated on this exact model and size. |

These look like Gemini uses but make no calls: `api/routes/lookup.py:64-70` only builds the lookup `Assessor`, which is out of scope. `api/routes/feed.py:92,101` and `web/trackdown/src/ui/format.ts:92` are UI text that names Gemini, and `analyst/pricing.py` is a price table.

## `api/routes/analyze.py`

It is user-facing: a synchronous FastAPI route, so a judge waits on the reply. It makes **0 Gemini calls per request**. The flow:

1. **Parse the input (`:86-89`).** `bsky_target` reads bsky.app and at:// links. A profile link joins the handle lookup.
2. **Look up the database (`:91-113`).**
   - Clusters for the handle, and for the raw and normalized URL.
   - Clusters for the text, if it yields a phrase of 5 or more words.
   - Clusters for a Bluesky post. If the post itself is in no cluster, the author's clusters are shown as context only.
3. **Live web check (`:116-128`).** This runs only for links that aren't Bluesky and are allowed for web checks, or for a text phrase. It calls `SourceChecker.check(adhoc=True)` (`sources/checker.py:46-85`), which makes at most 3 cached Oxylabs requests: scrape the link, search its headline, search the phrase.
4. **Reply (`:132-145`).** Either `matched`, carrying the analyst verdicts the worker already stored, or `insufficient`.

Nothing in this route needs to move to Nemotron.

## Reusing NemotronClient (`media/nemotron.py:250`)

- **What exists:** the only public method is `analyze(MediaInput)`. The private `_complete(messages, media_hash)` at `:346-407` is already generic over the messages. It has the rate limiter, retries, backoff and the Super VL model check, but it is keyed and logged by `media_hash`.
- **What's needed:** a text helper such as `chat_json(system, prompt, *, key)` is about 25–35 lines. It builds the system and user messages, calls `_complete`, then `parse_content` (`:172-185`, which already strips `<think>` blocks and code fences), and the caller validates the result as a `VerdictDraft`.

### What the backend contract needs that you didn't specify
1. **Pings:** `: ping` comment lines can't be seen by `EventSource`. The client switches to polling after 25 s with no message. That means a Gemini reading longer than 25 s ends up on polling. That still works, it just costs more requests. Sending `event: ping` with `data: {}` instead keeps the stream open, and the client already listens for it.
2. **First snapshot:** it must arrive within 4 s of opening the stream, or the client falls back to polling. That is how it detects a proxy that buffers.
3. **Headers:** send `Cache-Control: no-cache` and `X-Accel-Buffering: no`, and make sure Caddy doesn't compress or buffer `text/event-stream` responses.
4. **Snapshot `id`:** it must equal the job id; on a mismatch the client closes the stream and polls. Leave out `retry:`, because the client closes the stream on any error and doesn't reconnect.
5. **Readings order:** `readings[0]` should be the same object as `assessment`. The client uses `readings` when it isn't empty, otherwise `assessment`. Counter-evidence comes only from `assessment`. If `readings_disagree` is missing, the client compares the `llm_reading` values itself.
6. **Second-reading snapshot:** don't change posts, pages, edges or clusters in the same snapshot as the Gemini reading. Any change to those reloads the graph and refits it.
7. **Timeout:** the 150 s limit covers Gemini too. If it runs out after Nemotron's reading, or the job fails or returns 404 then, the UI keeps the readings it has and shows a toast. It does not fall back to the old analysis.

**What the tests cover (items 1–10)**
- **Nemotron reading:**
  - The assessment carries the model id the response returned, unknown cites are dropped, and the call is never a status.
  - The request sends the `json_schema` response format and `enable_thinking` off. The reasoning-on and unstructured options are covered too.
  - The timeout is clamped by `deadline`, with a 1 s floor once the deadline has passed.
  - A reply citing only unknown ids becomes "unclear", and a reply with `llm_reading: "matched"` is rejected.
- **Wrong model id:** `NotVisionModelError` is raised; run through a Lookup, the assess step fails and no reading or Nemotron receipt is stored.
- **Empty "length" reply:** raises `ValueError`. Through a Lookup, the assess step fails and the Gemini fake's reading becomes `assessment`.
- **Two readings:** when they disagree, both are kept, `readings_disagree` is True, the note is added, and the status is unchanged ("insufficient", or "matched" with `FakeStore`). A second reading that arrives first does not take over. Agreeing readings add no note.
- **Scheduling:** threading Events with a 2 s cap set the order, so a wrong order fails the test instead of hanging it. The X and web searches start before the author profile returns, and verify starts before a slow linked page from a t.co card finishes. For a web input, the markdown heading starts the searches before the fact extraction; the final page has role "linked" and the facts receipt.
- **Caps:** `verify_max` and `profiles_max` hold across repeated queue calls, an account already read is not read again, and only verified posts count as copies.
- **Cache:**

  - A repeat call through `CachedOxylabs` does not reach the inner client and is marked cached. Failures are not cached, and each thread keeps its own `last_call`.

- **SSE:** a finished job sends one `snapshot` event equal to the snapshot, then the stream ends; an unknown id gives 404. A scripted running job sends only changed snapshots and stops at the first non-running one.

to 8 copy pages, 1 linked page), 0-2 Nemotron calls and 1 Gemini call, in 20-40 s.'''
assert a in s
s = s.replace(a, '''A typical X post lookup makes 8-20 Oxylabs calls (1 post page, 1-5 profiles, 4 searches, up
to 8 copy pages, 1 linked page), 1-3 Nemotron calls (images and the reading) and 1 Gemini call.

## Timings (2026-11-14, live endpoints, seconds from the request)

Five real inputs (an X post, an X post with an image, an AP News Bluesky post, an AP article,
a sentence), 2 runs of the old phase order with Gemini's reading vs 3 runs of this one. Taken
from the steps' `started_at`/`ended_at`, the receipts' latencies and a 100 ms poll of the job
(what a client sees). Oxylabs latency varies a lot between runs (`/scrape` p50 3.6 s, p90 7.2 s).

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| First facts on screen (post, author or page), median | 2.1 s | 0.4 s |
| Web page: searches start | 7-12 s (after the AI fact extraction) | ~4 s (quick markdown headline) |
| The reading call | 10-21 s (Gemini) | 1.2-2.0 s (Nemotron, reasoning off) |
| The reading on screen, median (range) | 32.5 s (23-41) | 14.6 s (4.5-22; one run with a hung Oxylabs read, before the per-call caps, 52) |
| Job done, median (Gemini's second reading included) | 32.5 s | 31 s |
| Trackdown: backend change to screen | 1.1-3.6 s (1.5 s poll, waited for `done`) | 0.03-0.16 s (SSE) |

Where the remaining time goes: Oxylabs. `verify` (candidate copy pages, then each copier's
profile; ~3-5 s each) is now the long pole at ~7-12 s, then ~1.5 s for Nemotron's reading.
Nemotron with reasoning on took 7.5-15 s per reading and returned nothing once (all 8192
tokens spent reasoning), so it stays off; with reasoning off, 20 of 20 readings were valid JSON
(guided decoding), cited only real receipts, and made the same call as Gemini on 3 of the 4
lookups (the AP article: Nemotron "unclear", Gemini "organic_looking"). Every number in their
text traced back to a receipt (rounded counts, spans computed from the times).''')
p.write_text(s)
EOF
